text: In 1919, Boston was hit by a tsunami. Of syrup. A steel tank held over eight million litres of molasses. It leaked so badly that locals collected the drips. The company's fix? Paint the tank brown, so the leaks wouldn't show. On a warm January day, the overstressed steel split. A wave up to eight metres high rolled through the streets at over fifty kilometres an hour, and cold molasses only gets thicker. Twenty-one people were killed. The company blamed anarchists. The court blamed the tank. Paint is not a structural repair.
